newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Water supply and sanitation projects costing up to one billion rand will provide 1.7 million more people with running water by the end of the year, the water affairs and forestry department said.
- Primedia Ltd directors Mervyn King and Eric Ellerine have stepped down from the board amid talk that they were asked to resign for owning shares in rival media company Sasani.

- Industrial group Johnnic will have to achieve compound growth of 12 to 14 percent over the next five years if its black empowerment shareholder, the National Empowerment Consortium (NEC), is to retain its controlling stake, source said.

- Another Arican National Congress (ANC) leadership crisis in the Free State was defused when it was announced that former premier Patrick Lekota would not accept nomination as chairman of the provincial executive.

- The ANC would investigate setting aside a quota on its election lists for members of the Congress of South African Trade Unions and strengthening the union federation's representation on the organisation's national executive committee, acting secretary-general Cheryl Carolus announced.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The fraud at NBS Bank uncovered last week involved transactions of about 135 million rand, Tony Norton, the bank's chief executive said.

- Gengold, Gencor's gold division, posted its sixth consecutive boost in profit as distributable income moved ahead 20 percent to 68.9 million rand in the December quarter through higher production, a better gold price and a weaker rand, the company said.
- The Securities Regulation Panel is believed to have launched an investigation into possible insider trading in Automakers, the holding company of Nissan South Africa.
- A perjury charge has been laid against Donald Gordon, the chairman of Liberty Life, by a former employee who claims he was sacked for blowing the whistle on the misconduct of a company manager.

- The trade and industry department will apply for a $46 million loan from the World Bank, $21 million less than originally planned, for the part-financing of a project to improve comptetitiveness, according to the bank's local office.
SAKE-BEELD
- The Securities Regulations Panel has begun a probe of the possibility of insider trading in the shares of Automakers.
- Increased production, a higher gold price and lower working costs per kg raised Gengold's distributable income for the sixth consecutive quarter, managing director Tom Dale announced.

- The Africa International Trade Centre (AITC) has apparently not survived its first year because of financial difficulties after African states were unwilling to pay their membership fees. The body, which was intended to act as a focal point for economic cooperation in Africa, was opened in February last year.
THE STAR

- Desmond Tutu's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, given the task of healing South Africa's racially polarised society, has been gripped by racial tensions, with senior black officials saying it is run by "a clique of liberals" led by deputy chairman Alex Boraine.
- More than 200 cases of child rape are reported to police each week, of which at least 50 occur in greater Johannesburg.

- The ANC in the Free State has once again been thrown into disarray with the announcement by its national leaders that ousted premier Patrick "Terror" Lekota will not stand for the provincial chairman's position.
